items.title: Dinner: vegan ramen at T's Tantan, Tokyo Station
items.place: T's Tantan (Gransta Tokyo), Gransta Tokyo B1F (Square Zero area), JR Tokyo Station, 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0005
items.cuisine: Vegan ramen (sesame tantanmen, yuzu salt ramen, vegan gyoza)
items.halalSource: Fully vegan ramen shop (no meat, fish, egg or dairy). Beer is sold (Heartland ¥800). No pork or meat anywhere on the menu. (https://ts-restaurant.jp/tantan/)
items.hours: Every day 10:00 am – 10:00 pm (last order 9:30 pm)
items.note: Tight on 26 Dec: the Narita Express reaches Tokyo at 8:51 pm and the last order is 9:30 pm. If you are late, go to Soranoiro (the alternative, last order 10:30 pm). Keep the suitcases at the table if there is room, or use the large coin lockers next to Gransta (about ¥700–900). Order: Japanese Yuzu Sio (salt) Ramen ¥1,250 for a light bowl, or Golden Sesame Tantanmen ¥1,250 (not marked hot); skip the black sesame (hot) version; 3 or 6 gyoza to share. The shop moved on 1 Aug 2026 from Keiyo Street (inside the gates) to Gransta Tokyo B1F, outside the gates; older guides still give the old spot. Last order is 9:30 pm, so they must be in the queue by about 9:15 pm; arriving at Tokyo Station at 8:15 pm leaves enough time, but with only about 12 seats a Friday queue is possible. If the line is long, Soranoiro Nippon (Tokyo Ramen Street, same basement) is open until 10:30 pm. Inside the station basement, so no outdoor walk with luggage before dinner;
items.costBasis: ¥1,650 each: Japanese yuzu salt ramen or golden sesame tantanmen ¥1,250 + 3 vegan gyoza ¥400 (Oct 2026 menu)
items.rating: HappyCow 5.0 (1,071 reviews); Google and Tabelog not found
items.stepsWhy: About 4 min from the Narita Express platform to Gransta B1F

alts.cuisine: Ramen with a vegan menu (vegan ramen, vegan tantanmen, vegan gyoza)
alts.halalSource: Only the vegan bowls qualify; the shop also sells non-vegan ramen. Past reviewers said a 'vegetarian' broth contained shellfish or butter, so order an item labelled vegan. Alcohol not confirmed. (https://www.happycow.net/reviews/soranoiro-tokyo-120511)
alts.hours: Every day 9:00 am – 11:00 pm (last order 10:30 pm)

Tokyo Ramen Street is in the Yaesu-side basement, so the walk on to the hotel, lyf Ginza Tokyo (2-5-4 Kyobashi), is about 8-10 minutes via the Yaesu exit. Do not confuse it with the Soranoiro branch in Kyobashi, which serves pork tonkotsu ramen.
alts.costBasis: ¥1,400 each: one vegan ramen bowl (exact 2026 price not confirmed)
alts.stepsWhy: About 1 min closer each way than the planned meal

items.title: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Street, Asakusa

move.route: Walk 2 min to Kyobashi station, Ginza line to Asakusa (about 17 min), then the Kaminarimon gate is next to exit 1.
move.source: fare from the operator's fare table (IC card fare)

items.note: Tokyo's oldest temple, free. The grounds are always open; the main hall 6:00 am – 5:00 pm. Walk in through the Kaminarimon gate and its giant lantern, then Nakamise Street (souvenir and snack stalls, open about 10:00 am), the five-storey pagoda and the main hall. Sunday mornings get busy after 10:30 am, and the New Year stalls go up from late December.

items.note: Tokyo DisneySea is the pick: it exists only in Japan and suits adults (the Mediterranean harbour, Mysterious Island, Fantasy Springs; its 25th anniversary "Sparkling Jubilee" runs all year). Open 9:00 am – 9:00 pm on Tue 29 Dec; be at the gate by 8:30 am, as the year-end week is one of the busiest of the year. Shows on 29 Dec: Sparkling Jubilee Celebration 11:15 am, 1:45 pm and 3:45 pm, Believe! Sea of Dreams night harbour show 7:30 pm, "New Day, New Dreams" New Year fireworks 8:30 pm (from 26 Dec). Closed that day: Mermaid Lagoon Theater and Liberty Landing Diner. Use the Tokyo Disney Resort app for waiting times; Disney Premier Access (paid in the app on the day): Anna and Elsa's Frozen Journey and Soaring ¥2,500 each. Ristorante di Canaletto takes Priority Seating from 10:00 am Japan time on 29 Nov (3:00 am Cairo time). If you pick Disneyland instead: Harmony in Color parade 2:15 pm, Electrical Parade Dreamlights 7:00 pm, New Year fireworks 8:30 pm. No halal food in the parks; outside food is allowed only in the picnic area outside the gate (official FAQ), except for guests with dietary needs.

items.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha: the thousand red gates

items.note: Free and always open. Walk through the Senbon Torii tunnels of red gates to the Okusha prayer hall and on up the first stretch of gates, then back down (about 1.5 h). visas.costLabel: 10,000 EGP for two, cash on collection
visas.summary: Needed: Egyptians living in Egypt cannot use Japan's eVISA. Apply in person at the Embassy of Japan in Maadi; the embassy keeps the passports while it processes (at least 5 working days, not guaranteed; it advises 3 weeks ahead). For a 25 Dec departure there is time to wait for the China decision first: apply by about 6–10 Dec.
facts: 5,000 EGP (about US$93), paid in cash when you collect the visa. Multiple entry 10,000 EGP.

Minimum 5 business days, not guaranteed; may take longer depending on the case. The embassy strongly advises applying at least 3 weeks before departure. Results are announced by uploading the acceptance number on the embassy website.

For Fri 25 Dec: the embassy advises applying by about 4 Dec (3 weeks ahead); the minimum 5 working days means a complete file handed in by Thu 10 Dec should be back around Thu 17 Dec. The embassy closes for its own holidays on 30–31 Dec.

In person at the Consular Section, Embassy of Japan, 1st floor, 81 Corniche El Nil Street, Maadi, Cairo. No appointment needed for application or pickup. Sunday - Thursday 9:00 am - 2:00 pm (be at the gate at least 20 minutes before closing; security check). Closed Friday, Saturday and embassy holidays. Embassy holidays: 30–31 Dec. Documents cannot be sent by mail, fax or email. No designated agencies are mentioned; Egyptian citizens apply directly at the embassy.
A single-entry visa is valid for entry within 3 months from the date of issue.
Fill in Visit Japan Web before landing for the immigration and customs QR codes.
documents: Visa application form, filled in and signed (one per person)
1 recent passport-size photo, white background (damaged or old photos refused)
Certificate of employment showing salary, tenure and position (enrollment certificate for students)
Original stamped bank statement for the last 3 months, in English
If applying together as a family: proof of relationship (e.g. marriage certificate)
All Arabic documents need an English or Japanese translation attached; attach a copy of the flight, hotel and itinerary to each application; do not staple. Additional documents may be requested.

Lunch sets ¥1,200 - ¥2,200; closed Wednesday. Late-2026 status not confirmed: call 03-5246-6547. Halal: halal-certified (Halal Gourmet); halal soy sauce and rice seasoning.

items.place: Asakusa Sushiken, Asakusa (2-11-4 Asakusa)
items.why: Asakusa is known for tendon, and Sushiken serves a halal tendon of seafood and vegetable tempura at lunch (lunch menus ¥1,200 - ¥2,200; exact tendon price not confirmed). No halal-only tempura restaurant was found in Tokyo. Fried, so a heavier choice. Halal: halal-certified (Halal Gourmet).

items.place: Halal Wagyu Ramen & Beef Cutlet Shunpudou, Asakusa (2-6-11 Asakusa, 3F)
items.why: Crumbed A5 black wagyu cutlet set with rice, miso soup and cabbage, a Tokyo favourite that is normally not halal. It is on the same menu as the planned Asakusa lunch, so they can order it there instead of ramen. Fried, so a heavier choice. Price is the Savor Japan average lunch spend; menu prices are not published. Halal: halal-certified ingredients, no alcohol (official site).

items.dish: Ramen (halal wagyu ramen) (和牛ラーメン)
items.place: Halal Wagyu Ramen Shinjuku-tei, Shinjuku-sanchome (also Shibuya, Ginza, Asakusa, Ueno branches)
items.why: Halal take on Tokyo ramen with A5 wagyu; easy to fit in, branches all over central Tokyo. Halal ramen is in the plan: Shunpudou (Asakusa lunch, 27 Dec) and Shinjuku-tei branches as alternatives in Asakusa, Shibuya, Shinjuku and Gion. Halal: halal-certified chain, no pork or alcohol (body not named).

items.place: CHIBO Diversity Dotonbori Building, Dotonbori
items.why: Osaka's signature savoury pancake, from Chibo, a famous Osaka chain. This floor is the chain's Muslim and vegetarian branch, open 5:00 pm - 10:00 pm daily and 3 min from the Glico sign. Halal: Muslim-friendly: halal-certified ingredients, prayer room, vegetarian menu; not fully certified (HalalSpy 2026).

items.place: Creo-Ru Dotonbori main shop, Dotonbori
items.why: Osaka's street-food icon: one boat of 6-8 balls (¥600-950), crisp outside. The octopus is seafood, so only the sauce and oil matter. Honolu Grande Shinsaibashi (2-1-3 Shinsaibashisuji, halal certified) also makes halal takoyaki, but its hours were not confirmed. Halal: Travel guides (Japan Travel; Trip to Japan, Mar 2026) say the sauces and frying oil are halal and a chicken version exists; the certifier is not named, and other Creo-Ru branches are not halal.

items.dish: Shojin ryori (Zen temple vegetarian meal) (精進料理)
items.place: Shigetsu, inside Tenryu-ji, Arashiyama
items.why: Kyoto's classic temple food, served in a working Zen temple with a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand; vegetarian, so it fits the food rules, and good value at ¥3,800 plus ¥500 garden entry. Planned for lunch on 31 Dec (closed on Thursdays: see the day). Halal: vegetarian (no meat or fish; use of cooking sake not confirmed).

items.place: Honke Tankuma Honten, Kiyamachi, near Kawaramachi (not confirmed)
items.why: A MICHELIN-starred Kyoto kaiseki house with a certified halal course, the only true halal kaiseki found; but about ¥31,600 per person (undated blog price) is far over the ¥15,000 cap, so skip unless you want one big splurge. Halal meals need booking 2 days ahead. Far over their budget at about ¥31,600 per person, so skip unless they want one splurge. Halal: halal-certified course (Kyoto Council for Sharia and Halal Affairs, per a Rakuten Travel listing).

items.place: Saryo Tsujiri, Gion main store, Gion, Shijo-dori, about 3 min east of Gion-Shijo Station
items.why: The famous Uji-matcha parfait (Tokusen Tsujiri Parfait about ¥1,441), an easy add-on near the Gion dinner. Hours conflict between listings (10:30 am - 8:00 pm vs 11:00 am - 6:00 pm with Wed/Thu closed), so check. Nakamura Tokichi's Kyoto Station cafe is listed as temporarily closed for renovation; its Uji main store is the other option. Halal: unconfirmed (vegetarian dessert; jellies and ice cream may contain gelatin, ask).

items.dish: Wagashi (anmitsu, sweet bean and matcha sweets) (和菓子)
items.place: Asakusa Umegen, Asakusa
items.why: Traditional handmade sweets in Asakusa, an easy add-on if they dine at Panga. Masudaen Sohonten near Senso-ji is described by a reviewer as halal for matcha ice cream (not certified). Halal: halal-certified per Groovy Japan (body not named); hours, price and 2026 status not confirmed.

items.place: none found in central Tokyo
items.why: Yakitori is a classic Tokyo evening food, but no halal yakitori shop was found: byFood lists Wakaba and Toriyoshi with no halal certificate. Skip it; halal wagyu yakiniku at Gyumon Shibuya is the closest grilled-meat substitute. Halal: no halal-certified or Muslim-friendly yakitori shop found.

items.dish: Monjayaki / okonomiyaki (もんじゃ焼き / お好み焼き)
items.place: Tsukishima / Asakusa
items.why: Tokyo's own griddle dish, but no halal monja or okonomiyaki place was found; batters often use dashi and pork, and it is runny and oily. Skip. Halal: no halal-certified place found.

items.place: Shinsekai
items.why: A Shinsekai classic, but it is deep-fried and there is no reliable halal option, so skip it. Halal: No halal-certified kushikatsu restaurant could be confirmed; mainstream Shinsekai shops (Daruma and others) share fryers and serve pork.

considered.title: Etihad via Abu Dhabi: 1:50 pm Fri 25 Dec, back 5:20 pm Sat 2 Jan
considered.why: US$528 cheaper for two, but it lands at 11:40 am on 26 Dec and leaves Narita at 5:20 pm on 2 Jan, so the first and last days would change (Osaka Castle at 9:00 am and an earlier Shinkansen); Shady asked to keep the plan the same. Non-refundable (change fee from US$170; TripFlex US$232 each).

considered.why: Avoids the Shinkansen back to Tokyo on a busy New Year return day, but costs US$542 more for two than the Qatar round trip.

considered.title: Halal Wagyu Yakiniku Panga, Asakusa: A5 wagyu course
considered.why: A fully halal restaurant with no alcohol (the stricter wagyu choice), A5 yakiniku course ¥9,500 each plus service, but Saturday dinner would move from Shibuya back to Asakusa. The must-try wagyu dinner is the halal Kobe beef in Namba on 31 Dec instead.
facts: Ginza line Shibuya → Asakusa direct, about 30 min; then direct back to Kyobashi

considered.title: One night in Kyoto (Tokyo 4, Kyoto 1, Osaka 2)
considered.why: Three hotels in eight nights and pricier Kyoto rooms. Staying in Umeda keeps one hotel for both Kyoto days (29 min by JR, 45 min by Hankyu from Gion) and USJ (15 min), and the suitcases go ahead by courier.

considered.title: Sagano Romantic Train, Arashiyama
considered.why: Its 2026 season ends after 29 Dec, so it does not run on 31 Dec; Tripadvisor rates it 3.9.

considered.title: Umeda Sky Building, Floating Garden Observatory
considered.why: One viewpoint per city: Shibuya Sky is the paid one in Tokyo, and the Osaka evening went to Dotonbori. It is 10 min from the hotel if you want it on Thu 31 Dec or Fri 1 Jan (check New Year hours).
